items.title: Trump says Google rejected his idea to rename ocean after him
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday told supporters about his alleged attempt to have an ocean named after him and Google's refusal to go along with the idea, reported German news agency dpa. Speaking at a campaign rally in Georgia, Trump claimed he had suggested to representatives of the internet giant that either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean be renamed the "Trump Ocean". Trump told supporters he had sent Google a map labelled "Trump Ocean", but company representatives rejected the idea.

items.title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20. “Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party. The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

items.title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global maritime dispute resolution - Chief Justice
items.summary: He said Malaysia has long had a specialised Admiralty Court, and the establishment of the International Commercial and Admiralty Division (ICAD) has brought admiralty and international commercial cases under a single specialised division. Wan Ahmad Farid said that delays of even a few days in urgent admiralty cases could have significant commercial consequences, particularly when disputes involved vessels, cargo and parties across several jurisdictions. "Admiralty disputes are inherently international, involving vessel arrests, charterparty disputes, cargo claims, maritime security and arbitration.

items.title: Local cocoa production needs boost to cut import reliance
items.summary: MELAKA: Malaysia needs to boost local cocoa bean production to reduce reliance on imports, as the processing industry depends heavily on foreign supplies. Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said stronger local production was needed to strengthen the cocoa supply chain and ensure growers benefited from the industry's expansion. However, growth in cocoa processing needed to be matched by higher local bean production so growers could also benefit, she said when opening A Malaysian Cocoa Affair 2026, organised by the Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) at a shopping centre in Banda Hilir today.

items.title: Customs officer died from pressure to neck, post-mortem finds
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A post-mortem found that a female civil servant who was found murdered in Nilai on Thursday died from pressure applied to her neck. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the cause of death was determined following a five-hour post-mortem at the Forensic Medicine Department of Hospital Tuanku Ja'afar (HTJ) here today. The remains of Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, were brought out of the HTJ Forensic Medicine Department at 3pm immediately after documentation was completed.

items.title: 10 complaints lodged over suspected water-mixed RON95 petrol in Selangor
items.summary: Its director, Muhamad Hanif Asa'ari, said field investigations and enforcement operations at seven petrol stations yesterday were conducted in response to public complaints and reports on social media. However, he said notices under Section 32 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 had been issued, requiring petrol station operators to submit information and business-related documents to assist the investigation. "An investigation is being conducted into the possibility of violations of Section 5(1)(c), read together with Section 6(1)(d) and Section 7 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, relating to allegations of false trade descriptions concerning the petrol supplied," he said.

items.title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group. Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.

items.title: Pairin Kitingan writes life story to keep Sabah's history alive
items.summary: PENAMPANG: Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan wrote a 270-page autobiography to help his grandchildren understand his life and preserve key historical events in Sabah's history. The former Sabah chief minister said the idea came after realising that his grandchildren, particularly those studying in Australia, knew little about his life and contributions. Titled Joseph Pairin Kitingan, the book documents significant events in Sabah's history, including the 1982 Kaamatan harvest festival in Tambunan, when Pairin was told by the Berjaya government to resign from the state cabinet.

items.title: Trump blocking Russia sanctions a 'historic moment', says Putin envoy
items.summary: MOSCOW: US President Donald Trump's decision to waive a new package of sanctions on Russia is a "historic moment", a Russian presidential envoy said on Saturday. Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia's energy revenues, two days before they were due to take effect. "The Trump administration's suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment," Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.

items.title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest. Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action. “For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions.

items.title: Tanker hit off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, crew evacuated
items.summary: DUBAI: A tanker was struck by an "unknown projectile" off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, forcing the evacuation of its crew, a maritime monitoring agency said on Saturday. Vanguard, another maritime security agency, identified the ship as the Marshall Islands-flagged Safeen Principal crude oil tanker, saying it had lost power and suffered an engine-room fire. Oil prices have soared during the war.

items.title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal. Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15. “The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.

items.title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones. “All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.

items.title: Ramanan says Sungai Buloh seat secure amid strong grassroots support
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: Sungai Buloh member of parliament Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan considers his position in the constituency "safe", driven by strong support from residents. Ramanan, who is also the human resources minister, said he has done his best in fulfilling his responsibilities as an MP and will continue striving to enhance his performance to meet the community's expectations. Ramanan said the event was held as an open session without participant filtering or preset questions, allowing residents to freely air grievances and raise longstanding issues.

items.title: Armed forces to review reserve personnel allowances
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: The armed forces is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces. "Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel," he said.

items.title: Malaysia records 5,278 domestic violence cases, with numbers still climbing, says Nancy Shukri (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — A total of 5,278 domestic violence cases have been reported in Malaysia, with the number continuing to rise, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said the ministry was placing greater emphasis on counselling and women’s empowerment to help women better understand their rights, build confidence and achieve financial independence. https://www.facebook.com/borneopost.online/videos/a-total-of-5278-domestic-violence-cases-have-been-reported-in-malaysia-with-the-/1385867886638367/ Commenting on the recent case in Negeri Sembilan involving a 35-year-old female customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband, Nancy said the ministry was looking into providing assistance to the victim’s family and children.

items.title: TVET students to get training with job guarantees
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: The government will introduce an industrial training programme with job guarantees to improve the employability of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) students. He said an understanding had been reached to introduce the programme, which would include student exchanges. The Advanced Technology Training Centres (ADTEC) would send Malaysian students to partner institutions and receive students from them, including Singapore's Institute of Technical Education (ITE).

items.title: Penang Port becomes Malaysia's first port with private 5G network
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Penang Port Sdn Bhd (Penang Port) has become Malaysia's first port to deploy a private 5G network on dedicated spectrum, marking a significant milestone in its digital transformation toward becoming a smart port. Penang Port acting chief executive officer Fakhrul Azhar Tajudin said the network operates independently of the public commercial mobile network, with its 5G core and associated port applications hosted entirely within the port's premises. He said this gives the port operator greater control over network performance and operational data, while supporting data sovereignty, security, and low-latency communications.

items.title: Sarawakian couple allegedly paid three friends RM8,000 each to smuggle cocaine into Japan, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — A Sarawakian husband and wife allegedly recruited three friends to traffic cocaine into Japan, said Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan. The Star reported that each of the three friends was paid RM8,000 and was believed to have known they were carrying contraband. Hussein said the couple had invited their three friends on what was presented as a holiday in Japan.

items.title: Ports, railways and highways could be next in Malaysia’s 5G coverage push
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Oct 17 — The Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will study expanding telecommunications coverage targets, particularly for 5G, to include key economic areas such as ports, rail lines and highways. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the current Coverage of Populated Area (CoPA) metric should be reviewed to account for connectivity needs in areas with few or no residents but significant economic activity. “CoPA is frequently used by telecommunications companies and international bodies to refer to connectivity in populated areas.

items.title: Fahmi: Communications, Transport ministries to expand 5G coverage at major ports
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: The Communications Ministry will collaborate with the Transport Ministry to expand 5G network coverage across major ports nationwide. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the collaboration builds on previous joint efforts with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to resolve internet connectivity issues along main Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) rail routes. "Previously, the Communications Ministry and MCMC assisted in resolving internet coverage issues along major rail lines.

items.title: Perak studying elephant food bank proposal
items.summary: IPOH: The state government is studying a proposal to establish an elephant food bank to mitigate human-elephant conflict. State Science, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Teh Kok Lim said the proposal could involve creating buffer zones within elephants' roaming areas to provide them with an alternative food source. "We are currently studying the possibility of establishing a food bank for elephants.

items.title: Slain border agency officer’s remains to be buried in Tumpat tonight, says home minister
items.summary: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The remains of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency officer allegedly killed by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, underwent a post-mortem this morning before being transported to Tumpat, Kelantan, for burial. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad reportedly said police received information about the incident at 8.30pm that day. Meanwhile, Kampung Gosong here has received RM500,000 to upgrade public facilities and residents’ homes under the ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani initiative.

items.title: Taxi drivers thank government, say RM1,000 aid eases burden
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Taxi drivers in the state have thanked the government for a one-off RM1,000 cash assistance, saying it will help cover vehicle maintenance, daily expenses, and family needs. Taxi driver Mohamad Zahir Abd Razak, 55, who has been driving a taxi for more than 15 years, said the aid would help ease the burden of meeting daily expenses, maintaining his vehicle and supporting his children. Meanwhile, Penang Sentral taxi driver S. Kumaran, 54, said the funds would help support his family, including his 12-year-old child.

items.title: Motorists say RON95 wrecked their engines, and Selangor is now investigating seven petrol stations over watery fuel claims
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — Selangor is investigating seven petrol stations after motorists complained that RON95 petrol suspected of being contaminated with water had damaged their vehicle engines, following similar allegations in northern states earlier this month. Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the ministry had received 10 official complaints involving the seven premises and collected 27 petrol samples for laboratory analysis. Earlier complaints in northern states Earlier this month, Penang’s Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry office reported receiving 33 complaints involving about 30 petrol stations over alleged water contamination in RON95.

items.title: Family wants death in custody reclassified as murder
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A group of 80 people, including family members of a man who died in police custody, gathered at Bukit Aman today to submit a memorandum demanding the case be investigated as murder. LFL lawyers representing the family said Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, was arrested on Sept 20 and held at the Cheras police headquarters for 11 days. "Nooranis lodged two police reports on Oct 2 and 3 requesting a full investigation," an LFL representative told reporters outside Bukit Aman.

items.title: 'We have better things to do than set up khalwat traps' – Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR has denied allegations that the party is weaponising khalwat (close proximity) claims against rival political leaders to weaken opponents. PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari emphasised that PKR does not use personal issues as a basis for political rivalry. Meanwhile, commenting on preparations for the Melaka election, Amirudin, who is also Pakatan Harapan election strategy director, said PH is finalising several decisions.

items.title: Haze: Childcare centres remain open, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: KUCHING: No childcare centres (taska) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children's exposure to polluted air. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres takes into account the needs of working parents who rely on these services. She said parents have the discretion to decide whether to send their children to taska, particularly in areas where schools have been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.

items.title: Haze-hit areas: Parents to decide on childcare attendance, but kids must stay indoors, says family minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 17 — No taska (childcare centres) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children’s exposure to polluted air. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres took into account the needs of working parents who rely on the services. She said parents had the discretion to decide whether to send their children to childcare centres, particularly in areas where schools had been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index readings.

items.title: From neighbour disputes to legal reform, Malaysia moves to strengthen community mediation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN). Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Act, which falls under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), does not specifically cover the operation of JPNIN’s community mediation services. He cited Singapore’s Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India’s Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka’s Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.

items.title: RM1,000 aid to ease cost pressures on taxi, rental car drivers
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The government is stepping up efforts to help taxi and rental car drivers cope with rising operating costs and stiff competition, including a one-off RM1,000 aid for eligible drivers nationwide. "We know taxi drivers face various challenges, including rising vehicle spare parts costs and the cost of living. The assistance , introduced under the 2027 Budget, will benefit about 38,000 taxi and rental car drivers and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide.

items.title: Ministry studying Mediation Act amendments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Unity Ministry (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN). He said JPNIN's mediation services, including training and accreditation for community mediators, were currently based on Section 8(d) of the Rukun Tetangga Act 2012. He cited Singapore's Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India's Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka's Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.

items.title: Tired of dodging crow poop, Klang wants to put the birds on the pill
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 17 — After shooting nearly 6,000 crows this year, the Klang Royal City Council is weighing a different weapon against the birds of Bandar Bukit Tinggi: contraceptive bird feed. City councillor Chris Lee, who proposed the trial, said it would move the council away from culling towards a more humane way of controlling the population, The Star reported today. Shooting is only a short-term fix, Lee said, because new flocks keep arriving to exploit the same food sources.

items.title: Ranau and Kundasang roads buried in mud after heavy rain, authorities warn of more landslides
items.summary: RANAU, Oct 17 — Heavy rain on Thursday triggered mudflows and landslides at several locations around Ranau and Kundasang, leaving roads covered in mud, rocks and debris and prompting authorities to step up safety monitoring. The affected areas include Jalan Kundasang-Mohimboyon, Kampung Lipantai, Kibbas-Tambiau and the Mohimboyon-Kundasang Lama route, according to the Karanaan Community Development Leader’s Unit (UPPM). Ranau District Police Chief Supt Mursalin Mahmud urged residents and road users to remain vigilant, warning that continued rainfall could trigger flash floods and further landslides.

items.title: RM5 daily cap proposed as Tawau Hospital parking debate heats up
items.summary: TAWAU, Oct 17 — The proposed parking charges at Tawau Hospital should be viewed as a practical solution to persistent parking shortages and security concerns rather than a matter for continued debate. State Assistant Minister of Health, Women and People’s Wellbeing Datuk Rina Jainal said the provision of paid parking was intended to improve parking management, address concerns over accidents and theft, and enhance security for hospital visitors and staff. The Kukusan assemblywoman said the shortage of parking spaces at Tawau Hospital required practical solutions to ensure greater convenience for visitors and employees.

items.title: Indonesian fisherman found safe after 9 days adrift at sea
items.summary: KUANTAN: An Indonesian fisherman who went missing after his boat lost contact at sea was found safe near Pulau Tioman on Oct 15, nine days after departing from Indonesia. Pahang Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency director First Admiral Datuk Mazlan Mat Rejab said the boat had departed from Letung in Indonesia's Anambas Islands Regency on Oct 6 before contact was lost. "The Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre (MRSC) in Kuantan received information about the missing boat from its Indonesian counterpart via email on Oct 14.

items.title: Driver dies at scene after car crashes into Jalan Hang Tuah monorail pillar in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — A car veered off the road and slammed into a monorail pillar along Jalan Hang Tuah early this morning, killing the 28-year-old driver. According to Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Asst Comm Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, the fatal collision occurred at roughly 3.30am, as reported by The Star. The impact trapped the man inside the wrecked vehicle.

items.title: SAR operation underway for father, son feared lost in Besut forest
items.summary: Besut district chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the Search And Rescue (SAR) operation resumed at 8am, involving 38 personnel from various agencies and local villagers. He said the search team received information that Adam Adnan, 25, had managed to contact his family at about 10 am today and share their last known location in the forest. Mohd Rozaime said police received a missing persons report from the wife of one of the men yesterday, prompting the search operation.

items.title: Border control agency says inter-agency cooperation key to curbing illegal cross-border activities in Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 17 — Enforcement agencies must strengthen cooperation to ensue more comprehensive border control in Kelantan, especially in curbing cross-border activities through illegal routes. Rantau Panjang Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said it oversees five authorised entry points in Kelantan, while other enforcement agencies are responsible for areas that have not been gazetted, in accordance with their respective jurisdictions. Siti Khadijah said coordination between agencies was crucial to ensuring effective border control, especially in areas with illegal routes.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning in 9 states until 3pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 3pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, the whole of Penang, and several districts in Perak, namely Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Muallim, Kinta, Kampar and Batang Padang. In Selangor, the affected areas are Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat, while in Negri Sembilan, they are Seremban and Jelebu.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for nine states until 3pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 3pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, the whole of Penang, and several districts in Perak, namely Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Muallim, Kinta, Kampar and Batang Padang. In Johor, the warning covers Pontian, Kota Tinggi, Kulai, Mersing, Segamat and Johor Bahru.

items.title: DPM Zahid strengthens Malaysia-China ties, advances global TVET cooperation after five-day visit
items.summary: TIANJIN, Oct 17 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s five-day working visit to China has strengthened Malaysia-China strategic cooperation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), high-tech investment, security and disaster management, thereby opening new opportunities for human capital development and national economic growth. The October 12-16 visit also saw commitments to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductor, electric vehicles (EVs), nuclear technology and digital economy, while also strengthening bilateral ties under the Malaysia-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership framework. Malaysia also proposed the establishment of a World TVET Council as a platform to strengthen international cooperation, coordinate the sharing of best practices and drive the development a more integrated global skills ecosystem.

items.title: Laos drug jet case on agenda at Malaysia-Philippines meeting in Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police will raise the seizure of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos during a meeting with their Philippine counterparts in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, next week. "The meeting had been scheduled before the private jet was detained in Laos. Hussein said Malaysian police had already shared intelligence with Philippine authorities to help identify those behind the international drug trafficking operation.

items.title: Fadhlina: Police handling probe into suspicious packages at schools
items.summary: MELAKA: The Education Ministry is leaving the investigation into suspicious packages found at nine schools in Negri Sembilan to the police, says Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said the ministry remained vigilant about suspicious items found at schools nationwide and stressed the importance of prioritising school safety. Yesterday, Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed police received nine reports concerning suspicious packages found at several schools in Nilai and Tampin.

items.title: Suspicious packages at Nilai, Tampin schools: MOE leaves probe to police, says Fadhlina
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 17 — The Education Ministry (MOE) has left the investigation into the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Negeri Sembilan yesterday to the police. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry always adopts a vigilant approach towards the discovery of any suspicious items at schools nationwide. Yesterday, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that police had received nine reports concerning the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Nilai and Tampin.

items.title: Penang unveils Silicon Island Experience Centre as reclamation hits 200ha
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has reached a significant milestone in the Silicon Island project, with Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow making his first vehicular visit to the island and launching the Silicon Island Experience Centre today. He said the mega development would serve as a major catalyst for the state's economic growth over the next 50 years. "Silicon Island is not just another reclamation project, but a strategic catalyst for the state's economic growth for the next 50 years," he said during the visit.

items.title: Sister tells young nieces mother died of illness, withholds murder details
items.summary: TUMPAT: The elder sister of Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, told her two young nieces this morning that their mother had died, but withheld details of her death after she was found murdered at government quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA, Nilai, Negri Sembilan, on Thursday. Marliza Ibrahim, 48, said she told the children, aged five and six, that their mother had died of an illness rather than reveal the circumstances of her death. "When they asked why, I simply told them she was sick," she said.

items.title: Haze triggers highest alert level in southern Asean region
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Ongoing fires in Indonesia that have blanketed parts of Southeast Asia with toxic haze have triggered the highest-level alert by the regional bloc's climate and fire monitor. "Activation of Alert Level 3 for the Southern Asean region," the Singapore Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre said on its website, seen on Saturday. Based near Singapore's Changi Airport, the ASMC uses a four-tiered alert level system, from zero to three, with the highest triggered if there is a "high risk of severe transboundary haze in the region."

items.title: Children must not be stigmatised for life over birth status, says religious affairs minister
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a child should not be blamed for the circumstances of their birth, as Islamic principles clearly state that no individual bears the sins of another. He said that while legal rulings concerning lineage must be upheld, they should not be used as an excuse to subject children to social judgement. Zulkifli said society should also be mindful of the language used within families, educational institutions and administrative settings to avoid causing children to bear a prolonged social stigma.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Jeddah, Madinah flights tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah tomorrow. Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) said the decision follows a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment after temporary suspensions triggered by security concerns in Saudi Arabia. "For assistance, passengers can use the airline's Live Chat service or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 within Malaysia or +603 7843 3000 from overseas," it said in a statement.

items.title: Woman sending son to school killed as Hilux hits motorcycle in Kota Marudu; teen dies in separate Tawau collision
items.summary: Liza Jius, 34, died at the scene from severe head injuries, while her seven-year-old son, who was riding pillion and attends Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Marak Parak, sustained minor injuries. District Police Chief Supt Simiun Lomudin said the accident occurred at about 6.19am and involved the Modenas Kriss and a Toyota Hilux driven by a 40-year-old man. “The car’s 31-year-old female driver and 40-year-old female front passenger sustained minor injuries in the accident,” he told Daily Express .

items.title: Children must not be stigmatised over birth status - Minister
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a child should not be blamed for the circumstances of their birth, as Islamic principles clearly state that no individual bears the sins of another. He said that while legal rulings concerning lineage must be upheld, they should not be used as an excuse to subject children to social judgement. Zulkifli said society should also be mindful of the language used within families, educational institutions and administrative settings to avoid causing children to bear a prolonged social stigma.

items.title: Immigration detains 190 foreigners, two locals in Pudu entertainment centre crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Immigration Department detained 190 foreigners and two local men during a raid on an entertainment centre in Pudu here early today following public complaints about disturbances. Its Enforcement Division director, Datuk Basri Othman, said those detained comprised 99 men and 91 women, aged between 20 and 41. All those detained were taken to an immigration depot for investigation under Sections 6(1)(c) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines to resume Jeddah, Madinah services tomorrow after safety review
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flight operations to and from Jeddah and Madinah, Saudi Arabia, effective tomorrow (October 18) following a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment. “Passengers who made their bookings through third-party platforms or travel agents are advised to contact their respective booking providers directly regarding their travel arrangements,” it said in a statement today. Malaysia Airlines said customers requiring assistance could use the Live Chat feature on its website or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 (within Malaysia) or +603 7843 3000 (international).

items.title: Motorist escapes injury after tree branch falls on car in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 17 — A 31-year-old motorist escaped unhurt after a tree branch fell onto his Perodua Myvi in front of the Kuala Kangsar Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) office this morning. Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 8.57am, prompting seven personnel from the Kuala Kangsar Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene. Sabarodzi said firefighters used a chainsaw to remove the fallen branch, and the operation ended at 9.20am.

items.title: Loke: We cannot stop foreigners from using public buses, but all passengers must comply with rules
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The government cannot stop foreigners from using public buses, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said today when asked about complaints of unruly behaviour by foreigners on buses. “We cannot stop foreigners from taking public buses,” he said. “Public buses are public transport and everyone has the right to use them,” Loke said at a press conference after launching Rapid Penang’s electric buses at the depot in Weld Quay here.

items.title: Exercise freedom on social media with respect, courtesy, says King
items.summary: Sultan Ibrahim, who is also Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Chancellor, said this in response to the misuse of social media by certain quarters to incite others, spread hatred and sow division in society. Sultan Ibrahim was speaking at the 105th UiTM Convocation Ceremony at the Tuanku Canselor Grand Hall, UiTM Shah Alam, here today. Also present was Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who is also UiTM Pro-Chancellor.

items.title: Putrajaya mulls longer jail terms, higher fines for rail cable theft to protect public safety, says Loke
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The Transport Ministry is working with the Home Ministry on legal amendments to impose heavier penalties for cable theft affecting the country’s rail networks, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said today. “The details have not been finalised,” Loke said. Loke said the problem extended beyond the MRT network, with other rail operators, including Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad, also affected.

items.title: Loke: Rapid Penang starts electric bus services with 15 vehicles, targets 75 by March 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — Rapid Penang began operating its first 15 electric buses today, marking the start of its transition towards an electric bus fleet, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke today. According to a statement issued by Rapid Bus, the first procurement phase involved 250 electric buses across Rapid Penang and Rapid KL, with 175 allocated to the latter. Under the first stage, Loke said Rapid Penang would receive 40 buses and Rapid KL 110.

items.title: Nik Nazmi confirms he was one of two caught in Petaling Jaya Jais raid, apologises to wife and family
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Bersama leader Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad has confirmed that he is one of the two individuals involved in an incident with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) in Petaling Jaya on Thursday. In a statement addressing the incident, Nik Nazmi admitted his fault and confirmed that he was the man caught with a woman, who is not his muhrim (a legally permissible close relative), in an enclosed space. The statement was issued publicly by Nik Nazmi in response to reports regarding the Jais operation.
